stories.headline: Vikings left at QB crossroads after Carson Wentz's poor MNF showing vs. Bills
stories.summary: After a historically poor performance by Carson Wentz on Monday night, Vikings coach Kevin O'Connell was asked whether the team might trade for a QB ahead of Tuesday's deadline. He deferred the question to GM Nolan Teasley.
stories.body:
MINNEAPOLIS -- A horrific offensive performance on "Monday Night Football," fueled by the worst performance by a starting quarterback in the NFL this season, has put the Minnesota Vikings at a crossroads.

Having lost consecutive games after a 6-0 start, will they use the Tuesday afternoon NFL trade deadline to add a quarterback? Or will they try to make it work for the rest of this season with a combination of Kyler Murray, Carson Wentz and Max Brosmer?

Coach Kevin O'Connell deferred the question to general manager Nolan Teasley after Monday night's 23-6 loss to the Buffalo Bills. It was the third game this season that the Vikings failed to score a touchdown, a level of production that has threatened to waste high-level play from their defense and special teams.

"We've had dialogue about a lot of different positions," O'Connell said. "Tight turnaround, obviously, playing the Monday night game, and we'll get right to work on any potential moves that can be there. But really just focused on the game tonight, which was not good enough in any way, shape or form."

Wentz completed only 8 of 25 passes for 81 yards while throwing two interceptions and having a third dropped. His 2.3 QBR was the lowest for any quarterback this season and the lowest by a Vikings quarterback since Tarvaris Jackson recorded a 1.8 QBR during a game in 2006. It was also the lowest in a "Monday Night Football" game since Sam Darnold posted a 1.1 QBR in 2019 while playing for the New York Jets against the New England Patriots, a game where he was recorded saying he was "seeing ghosts."

"I haven't had many starts over the last couple years in general," Wentz said, "but this one felt pretty terrible. I'm not going to lie. Yeah, this one wasn't my favorite, that's for sure."

Wentz opened the game with multiple misfires on easy passes, and O'Connell said he "tried a bunch of tools to see if we could help that happen." O'Connell said he wanted the Vikings' offense to be balanced and that he did not want Wentz to be only passing in must-throw situations such as third downs. O'Connell admitted afterward that was a mistake, as Wentz finished with an off-target rate of 38% -- the lowest in an NFL game this season.

"I should have run the football more," O'Connell said, "and then just lived out those third downs. We only had eight of them because we didn't possess the football enough, but also because when we did get first downs, it was trying to see if we could get some completions, move the football and then get a good mixture going. Just not good enough."

Instead, Vikings running backs Aaron Jones Sr. and Jordan Mason combined for only 11 carries among 46 total plays.

Asked if calling offensive plays has ever felt as challenging as it does now, O'Connell said: "No."

The Vikings' 11 touchdowns this season are tied with the winless Los Angeles Chargers. Minnesota is the first team to have at least six wins, and at least three games without a touchdown, over its first eight games of a season since 1925.

The Vikings' performance has regressed as they have hit midseason. They managed to hold possession for only 17:28 on Monday night, following a mark of 24:17 in a 19-15 loss last week to the Detroit Lions, leaving most players to suggest that there is more going on than just poor quarterback play.

Tight end T.J. Hockenson was among multiple offensive players who were still wearing their full uniforms when reporters entered the locker room. Asked if he thought there was a quarterback on the team who could turn around the Vikings' offense, Hockenson paused for three seconds.

"I mean, I believe in our quarterback room," Hockenson said. "I believe in who those guys are. I'm with them every single day. I know how good, how talented that room is, and I know who those guys are. We just got to make some things shake on Sundays. It's really all it is."

Receiver Justin Jefferson once again appeared frustrated during the game. He skipped his postgame interview after last week's game in Detroit, but on Monday night, he suggested that the Vikings might benefit by simplifying their scheme.

"We've got to find ways to simplify it," Jefferson said, "and make it easier for everybody to just go out there execute the plays, not thinking, and just going out there and playing ball. We have the talent, and we have the guys in the room and on the offensive side of the ball to make plays and make something happen. We've just got to make the plays."

stories.headline: Ivar Stenberg leads the Sharks past the Islanders 3-2 in a shootout to stop their 5-game skid
stories.summary: — Ivar Stenberg scored the only goal in a shootout that lasted eight rounds, and the San Jose Sharks beat the New York Islanders 3-2 on Monday night to snap a five-game losing streak.
stories.body:
SAN JOSE, Calif. -- — Ivar Stenberg scored the only goal in a shootout that lasted eight rounds, and the San Jose Sharks beat the New York Islanders 3-2 on Monday night to snap a five-game losing streak.


Tyler Toffoli had a goal and an assist, and Stenberg also scored in regulation for the Sharks (8-11-1). Stenberg has six goals and is tied for the scoring lead among NHL rookies.


Yaroslav Askarov made 30 saves for San Jose.


Ben Hutton and Victor Eklund scored for the Islanders (7-6-4), who have lost four straight games (0-2-2). Ilya Sorokin stopped 37 shots.


Stenberg put the Sharks on the board late in the first period after Toffoli sent a shot toward the net. Stenberg got a piece of the puck to redirect it past Sorokin and tie the game at 1.


San Jose again rallied from a goal down midway through the second when Toffoli’s shot deflected off Islanders defenseman Adam Pelech and into the net. It was Toffoli’s first goal in eight games.


Hutton opened the scoring early in the first after Simon Holmstrom’s pass found him with an open look.


Eklund put New York ahead 2-1 early in the second with a power-play goal. Sharks center Alexander Wennberg, who returned after missing 10 games, was called for the penalty that led to the power play.


The game got chippy late in the second as fights broke out, leading to four five-minute major penalties. Barclay Goodrow received a penalty for fighting Mitchell Chaffee, and Ty Dellandrea was penalized for fighting Kyle MacLean.


Up next
Islanders: Visit the Los Angeles Kings on Thursday night.


Sharks: Host the Pittsburgh Penguins on Wednesday night.

stories.headline: Transfer rumors, news: Man United eye move for Forest's Murillo
stories.summary: Manchester United are in the relegation zone and are looking to improve their defense in January. Transfer Talk has the latest.
stories.body:
Manchester United want to bolster their defense with the signing of Nottingham Forest defender Murillo, while both Chelsea and Tottenham Hotspur are looking at signing Lens defender Ismaëlo Ganiou, Join us for the latest transfer news and rumors from around the globe.

Transfers home page | Men's summer grades | Women's grades

Trending rumors

- Football Insider reports that Manchester United want to bolster their defense with the signing of Nottingham Forest defender Murillo. The Brazil international, 24, joined from Corinthians in 2023 for around €6 million, but his transfer could be worth 10 times that now. United are also reported to be interested in Manchester City left back Rayan Aït-Nouri. The Red Devils were surprise suitors for the 25-year-old late in the summer, when it appeared an exit from City could be on the cards, and if they pull off a January deal it would be a rare cross-city move -- one that hasn't happened directly between the rivals since 2012.

- Chelsea and Tottenham are among a whole host of teams tracking the future of Lens defender Ismaelo Ganiou, according to TEAMtalk. The 21-year-old center back has been with the French club since last summer, making 37 senior appearances in that time as he continues to develop. That has caught the eye of the two London clubs, which are looking to invest in the backline for the future, while Paris Saint-Germain, Manchester City, Newcastle United, Fulham, and Brentford are also named as clubs that have been keeping an eye on Ganiou's progress.

- United have also been busy scouting other potential transfer targets in the market, according to Nicolò Schira, after attending a match between Atalanta and Monza. The club have been monitoring Atalanta goalkeeper Marco Carnesecchi, 26, who has a deal that expires in 2028, and Monza striker Gustavo Varela, with the 21-year-old being linked with a host of different clubs after scoring nine goals in 10 Serie A appearances.

- Fabrizio Romano has ruled out a potential move away from Inter Miami for Lionel Messi. The 39-year-old has recently been linked with a possible return to Newell's Old Boys in Argentina, one of the first teams he played for as an academy star, to see out his career. But with a contract that runs until 2028, Messi is set to stay in MLS for the next two years before considering his next possible options.

ESPN sources
- United States coach Mauricio Pochettino is the main candidate to replace Michael Carrick as Manchester United manager, with the club ready to sack the 45-year-old amid the team's struggles in the Premier League relegation zone, sources have told ESPN. Read

- Ronald Araújo wants to wait until the end of the season before he makes a decision on a permanent move to Liverpool. The Reds have a clause in his loan from Barcelona that could seal a permanent switch for €55 million, which could be triggered as early as January. (Sport)

- Kostas Tsimikas is expected to leave Liverpool next summer when his contract expires. The Reds are already looking at options to replace the Greece international left back, while Milos Kerkez is first choice. (Football Insider)

- Premier League clubs are showing an interest in AC Milan striker Alphadjo Cissè, 20, but the Italian side are looking to seal a new contract with the youngster. (Nicolò Schira)

- Napoli will listen to offers for Kevin De Bruyne in January, with the attacking midfielder approaching the final months of his contract with the Serie A side. (Ekrem Konur)

- Everton striker Thierno Barry is attracting attention in the transfer market, with Newcastle, Crystal Palace, RB Leipzig, and Como all following the Frenchman's progress. The 24-year-old has scored six goals in ten Premier League appearances this season. (Ekrem Konur)

- Eintracht Frankfurt are pushing to sign PSG right back David Boly. The 17-year-old defender has enjoyed a breakthrough campaign so far, which is attracting interest from elsewhere, while his contract expires next summer. (Florian Plettenberg)

- AC Milan will terminate the loan of David Odogu at Toulouse, with the 20-year-old center back looking to move elsewhere in the January transfer window. (Florian Plettenberg)

stories.headline: From an ACL tear to a time trial PB: Koby LeCras on building resilience in his draft year
stories.summary: Rangey wing-forward Koby LeCras saw a breakout year derailed by a partially torn ACL, but six weeks back running was enough to deliver a personal-best 2km time. He talks to Jasper Chellappah about his recovery and future ahead of the 2026 AFL Draft.
stories.body:
Koby LeCras wasn't expected to test at the AFL Draft combine. He also wasn't expected to be named best afield amongst the premier prospects of the 2026 draft class, or make his senior WAFL debut in his dad's No. 20 for West Perth.

It was a blazing start to his season that put the nephew of former West Coast forward Mark firmly in first-round contention. From there it all unravelled.

LeCras suffered a partially torn ACL in that WAFL debut. Senior football, the national championships, and flag tilts were all wiped away. It was a cruel end to a year that promised so much.

But the teenager was desperate to get back for something on his calendar, and the final destination for all draft hopefuls is the combine.

Despite just six weeks of training post-injury, LeCras turned out for the 2km time trial. He ran a 6:23, good for a top-15 time and a personal best under heavy duress.

"Going into it I had 6:25 written on my hand, so I got away with a couple seconds," LeCras told ESPN.

"When I started running it was the goal to do the 2km and the 20m sprint at the combine. I knew what the plan was, where I was going to be and what I was going to do."

Worries had been lurking at the back of Lecras's mind. He avoided surgery on the partial tear but it was difficult for him to regain 100% confidence in his knee when he got back to running.

"You look at Gryan Miers, you can rush it back. Being your draft year and you've obviously got a lot more footy to play than just this year [West Perth] were pretty quick to shut that down, that I wasn't going to play again.

"I just wanted to get back as quick as I could, whether it was combine or day one of pre-season. They said 'Yeah you can do the combine and then definitely back for day one of pre-season'."

LeCras's injury was devastating timing given the showing he'd treated recruiters to the previous week. Off a wing, the 192cm utility was best afield for the AFL Academy - a representative side featuring the best of the draft class thrown together against VFL opposition.

LeCras kicked three goals from 19 disposals and nine marks, commanding the air and showing off that aerobic endurance in defence and attack.

It was a performance reminiscent of Ollie Dempsey's ability to capitalise on mismatches with his strong hands in marking contests and sniff out opportunities in dangerous areas.

LeCras was delivering on the next evolution of the winger in the AFL, but he was playing up the ground out of team need and still sees himself as a forward 50 threat.

"I think I'm a natural forward, but I'm open to playing anywhere, whether it's halfback, wing, hopefully inside one day maybe.

"I love watching specific players, I'm probably a bit of a nuff.

"I love watching Jeremy Cameron, I reckon he's a superstar. And then obviously Logan Morris as well, sort of that undersized key forward. I love what he does and how he finds ways to beat his defenders. He's a freak, he's next level."

Koby's uncle Mark LeCras is one of the more underrated small forwards to play in the modern era. The one club player booted 441 goals from 219 games, and was the oldest player in the Eagles's 2018 triumph before retiring.

Similarly to his uncle, Koby is adept at twisting onto his preferred left foot and finding the goals from uncanny positions. He possesses natural forward craft, from leading patterns at challenging size to match up on to a natural, repeatable set shot action and goal nous from tight angles.

While his dad Brent enjoyed his own 141-game WAFL career, Koby's uncle continues to be a wealth of information as he prepares to step up to the AFL level.

"He's been massive. In the pre-season I watched a lot of vision with him, little ways to improve my game," LeCras said.

"If I could be half the player he was, I'd be really happy with that."

Mark's best day came against Essendon in 2010 at Etihad Stadium, kicking 12 goals straight. He booted 46 goals from 15 games against the Bombers in his career.

"We always joke about that, if he played against Essendon every week he would've kicked a thousand. That's what he reckons!"

stories.headline: Tigers SS Kevin McGonigle, Reds 1B Sal Stewart win MLB's rookie of year awards
stories.summary: Detroit Tigers shortstop Kevin McGonigle, 22, won the American League Rookie of the Year award Monday night in a televised presentation, moments before Cincinnati Reds first baseman Sal Stewart, 22, was honored as the National League Rookie of the Year.
stories.body:
Cincinnati Reds first baseman Sal Stewart was named the National League Rookie of the Year, and Detroit Tigers infielder Kevin McGonigle won the award in the American League on Monday, a crowning achievement for two young stars who shined in different ways.

McGonigle, a hard-nosed, Pennsylvania-raised left-handed hitter who excelled at plate discipline and avoided the prolonged slumps of a typical rookie season, received 28 of 30 first-place votes from the Baseball Writers' Association of America. Stewart, a brash, gifted slugger who was among the game's best at driving in runs, garnered 20 of 30 first-place votes in the NL.

New York Mets right fielder Carson Benge (seven) and St. Louis Cardinals second baseman JJ Wetherholt (three) got the rest of the NL first-place votes. Cleveland Guardians starter Parker Messick (two) received the remaining AL first-place votes. Boston Red Sox starter Payton Tolle, the third Rookie of the Year finalist in the AL, got 12 third-place votes.

McGonigle brought uncommon consistency and discipline for a 22-year-old who is only three years removed from high school, leading the AL with 7.1 Baseball-Reference wins above replacement and finishing fifth in the league in walks and hits. McGonigle became the first rookie to finish within the top five in both categories since Ted Williams in 1939, according to ESPN Insights.

The 2026 Tigers fell well short of expectations and were ultimately forced to trade star pitcher Tarik Skubal, a pending free agent, at midseason, but McGonigle, who signed an eight-year, $150 million extension midway through his first month, was a reminder of the young position player talent rising through the organization. While splitting time between shortstop and third base, McGonigle slashed .278/.376/.430 with 18 home runs, 12 stolen bases and almost as many walks (95) as strikeouts (100). His 97 runs scored led all rookies, and his 168 hits were tied with Benge for the lead among first-year players.

"Believing in myself and always seeing myself where I'm at today is what makes me most proud," McGonigle said on a conference call. "All the work I've put in, just to get to the point of where I'm at today."

Stewart, 22, brought premium power production to a short-handed Reds lineup, accumulating 32 home runs and 112 RBIs while putting together the first season of at least 30 homers and 100 RBIs for a Reds rookie.

A first-round pick out of high school in Miami in 2022, Stewart slashed .263/.330/.457 despite struggling in September and also added 15 stolen bases. He became just the fifth rookie to put up at least 100 RBIs and 15 stolen bases, according to ESPN Insights, joining Carlos Beltran (1999), Jose Canseco (1986), Tony Lazzeri (1926) and Al Simmons (1924).

His greatest source of pride, though, came from playing in all 162 games.

"The people around my corner, they understand how hard that is, how difficult that is," Stewart said. "Being available for your teammates every single day -- that's something that kind of goes unnoticed at times. But I know my teammates always appreciate that, and I want them to know I'm always there for them."

McGonigle and Stewart celebrated their achievement in their respective hometowns, with watch parties consisting of roughly 70 friends and family members.

They were the headliners of what proved to be a standout rookie class.

It also featured Messick, who went 12-9 with a 2.56 ERA in 32 starts for the Guardians. Tolle, the affable, mustachioed left-hander who put up a 3.03 ERA and struck out 171 batters in 148⅔ innings. Benge, who batted .282 while becoming the first Mets rookie to put up a 20/20 season. And Wetherholt, who combined elite defense with 17 homers and 14 steals. Munetaka Murakami, Carter Jensen, Chase DeLauter, TJ Rumfield, Logan Henderson and Nolan McLean also stood out, among several others.

Someday, they might help make up the new faces of the sport.

stories.headline: A timeline of how Donald Trump, Dana White forged friendship through the fights
stories.summary: Donald Trump and Dana White's friendship is on display cageside, on political stages and at the White House.
stories.body:
Editor's note: This story has been updated after originally being published in June 2026 before the UFC Freedom 250 event at the White House.

THE 28TH INSTALLMENT of the Ultimate Fighting Championship was a trial run. Though 36 states had banned the UFC, the New Jersey State Athletic Control Board allowed the then-owner, Semaphore Entertainment Group, to host its first sanctioned event on Nov. 17, 2000, at the Taj Mahal in Atlantic City, a hotel and casino owned by real estate mogul Donald Trump.

Fighter Randy Couture returned to the UFC for the first time since 1997 and recaptured his heavyweight championship against Kevin Randleman in the main event, but the most consequential appearance that night happened in the crowd of 5,000 fans.

Dana White attended, not as a UFC official but as the manager of fighter John Lewis. White was with friends Lorenzo Fertitta and Frank Fertitta III, brothers who were Las Vegas casino owners and trained in jiu-jitsu under Lewis. As they soaked in the atmosphere, they discussed all the things they could do when the Fertittas' company, Zuffa LLC, owned an MMA promotion.

Three months later, White returned to Atlantic City as UFC president at Trump's Taj Mahal for UFC 30.

That was a launching pad for the UFC and the beginning of a 25-year friendship between Trump and White that has led to Trump attending numerous UFC events, including four as a sitting president, and White introducing presidential candidate Trump at two Republican National Conventions.

"He is one of my very good friends," White told ESPN before the UFC held a fight card at the White House in June, adding that Trump is one of 10 friends in his small circle. "Like, you have a group of friends in your life that are, especially at my age, you've gone through all the s--- in your life and all this stuff. Me and this guy have been friends for 25 years and ... our relationship gets stronger every year."

On June 14, Trump's 80th birthday, their friendship reached a new landmark when the White House hosted UFC Freedom 250. Presidents have invited championship teams to visit the White House, hosted amateur games on the South Lawn and played tennis or basketball there themselves. But the UFC card was unprecedented -- a live professional sporting event staged on the White House grounds. ESPN combed through archival content from dozens of outlets to present the many ways two careers have crossed, creating a path for UFC fighters to walk into the Octagon on the South Lawn of the White House.

The timeline continues into the fall, with Trump inviting White to join his administration as press secretary. Or not.

• Jan. 11, 2001: Zuffa LLC purchases the UFC for $2 million and appoints White as the promotion's president. After having trouble landing a venue to host the UFC's two upcoming events, Zuffa makes a deal with Trump to host UFC 30 and UFC 31 back at the Taj Mahal in Atlantic City.

In all the years since, White has repeatedly expressed appreciation for Trump welcoming his company, saying the casino owner's involvement legitimized the UFC. "None of the venues wanted this," White told CBS's "60 Minutes" in 2025. "They didn't believe in it, they didn't like it, and they were worried about the type of crowd that would show up for this type of event."

After Trump stepped up, White remembered the time this way: "When the Trump brand was here [White holds his hand high overhead] and the UFC brand was down there [holding his hand near the floor], he saw it and said, 'I'd love to have it at my casino.'"

However, Trump's casino business faced severe financial problems at the time. According to PBS's "Frontline," his Atlantic City operation reported a net loss of $133.8 million for the 1999 fiscal year. The umbrella company holding the casinos filed for bankruptcy twice within the following decade.

• Feb. 23, 2001: The first event under Zuffa ownership, UFC 30, is at the Taj Mahal. In the main event, Tito Ortiz successfully defends his light heavyweight championship by slamming Evan Tanner unconscious in 30 seconds. White later said Trump was in attendance all night long at UFC 30 and UFC 31, also at the Taj Mahal, though ESPN could not find visual evidence of it, and the account has been disputed by multiple former UFC employees.

• June 29, 2001: The promotion's next fight card is at 20,000-seat Continental Airlines Arena, the East Rutherford home of the New Jersey Nets and Devils. For the first time, photos and the broadcast show Trump cageside. The UFC then books its next two fight cards in Las Vegas, at Mandalay Bay Events Center and at MGM Grand Garden Arena. White reflected on Trump's early support of the UFC in a 2011 interview, saying, "The guy saw this thing coming, was into it and gave us our first shot, and you'll never hear me say anything bad about Trump."

• Feb. 28, 2003: UFC 41 is held at Atlantic City's Boardwalk Hall, which has nearly three times the seating capacity of the Taj Mahal. Heavyweight Tim Sylvia and lightweight BJ Penn successfully defend their titles. Trump Plaza serves as the corporate host for the event, and the Taj Mahal casino features $5 chips with the UFC headliners' faces on them.

• Oct. 22, 2004: The UFC is back at Boardwalk Hall for UFC 50. It is headlined by Ortiz against a short-notice opponent, but the event is best known for being the card on which Georges St-Pierre first fights for a UFC title. St-Pierre loses to Matt Hughes. Also in the building is a production crew for the soon-to-debut reality TV show "The Ultimate Fighter." When TUF aired months after "The Apprentice" made Trump a reality TV darling, the show launched White to stardom, as well. A USA Today story drew a comparison, saying TUF had cast White in the "Donald Trump role."

• June 5, 2008: Trump calls a news conference at Trump Tower in Manhattan to announce a partnership with a startup MMA promotion, Affliction Entertainment, a venture of the Affliction clothing brand. The new promotion's star is heavyweight Fedor Emelianenko, widely considered the best MMA fighter in the world.

The Affliction brand had a long sponsorship history with the UFC, but when word got out that this new fight promotion was about to launch, the UFC banned its fighters from wearing Affliction clothing. At the introductory news conference, Trump acknowledges the potential competition between the UFC and Affliction by raising a topic that exists to this day in MMA: fighter pay. "If there's only one organization," he says, "you can pay the fighters five dollars and they'll be happy to fight."

However, Trump is not critical of the UFC boss. "I have great respect for Dana White," he says. "Some of the people in the room may not like him. I like him and I think he's done a very good job."

• July 19, 2008: Affliction Entertainment holds its first MMA event at the Honda Center in Anaheim, California, cheekily named "Affliction: Banned." It is headlined by Emelianenko knocking out former UFC heavyweight champion Tim Sylvia in 36 seconds. Two other former UFC heavyweight champs, Andrei Arlovski and Josh Barnett, fight on a card filled with talent signed away from the UFC. Megadeth, interrupting an international tour of summer music festivals, performs during the $39.99 pay-per-view.

Trump is asked afterward whether he thinks Affliction will take over MMA from the UFC. "I think it probably will," he says. "All the fighters want to be with us. I think it probably will take over."

That same night, the UFC holds a hastily scheduled fight card on five weeks' notice, made available on basic cable outlet Spike TV. The main event features a rare non-PPV appearance by the UFC's best fighter, Anderson Silva. White refuses to call this scheduling move counterprogramming, saying simply he is "giving the fans what they want."

• July 24, 2009: Almost exactly a year after its first MMA event, Affliction Entertainment folds. The abrupt end comes after one of the headliners on the promotion's third scheduled fight card, Josh Barnett, fails a steroid screening. Hours after the cancellation of "Affliction: Trilogy," the company announces it no longer will promote fights and instead will return as a clothing sponsor for the UFC.

This development shows White's business vision. At the UFC postfight news conference following Silva's KO win a year earlier, on the same night as Affliction's debut card, White had downplayed Affliction's chances of success, saying, "I figure after tonight those guys will be out of business." Asked why, White added, "Because they spent a lot of money tonight. And I know more about this business than they do. When you spend a lot of money and you don't get that money back, you usually go out of business."

White never mentioned Trump's name in his criticism of Affliction.

• Aug. 18, 2011: The UFC announces a seven-year, $700 million broadcast deal with Fox. White later revealed that Trump sent him a copy of a New York Times writeup about the deal with a note written on it that says, "Congratulations, Dana. I always knew you were gonna do it."

• Nov. 15, 2015: Hours after Holly Holm knocks out Ronda Rousey in a huge upset at UFC 193, Trump posts on X (then known as Twitter): "Glad to see that @RondaRousey lost her championship fight last night. Was soundly beaten - not a nice person!" Months earlier, Rousey had said she was voting for Bernie Sanders and downplayed Trump to CNN: "I don't want a reality TV star to be running my country." Rousey does not respond to Trump's "not a nice person" comment. Years later, she revealed that White asked her in 2016 not to speak badly of Trump. She said she agreed "because I owe Dana my life."

• Dec. 11, 2015: For the first time publicly, White backs Trump's presidential campaign. "Donald will get my vote," White says in an interview with TMZ.

• July 11, 2016: Steven Cheung, the UFC's director of communications and public affairs, leaves the promotion to join Trump's political campaign. Cheung had managed messaging for the UFC and its outspoken CEO since 2013. "When you're in communications, and you have a Dana White-type person, I think he would have learned a lot from that," UFC vice president of regulatory affairs Marc Ratner told NOTUS. "And that may have helped him there with the president."

• July 19, 2016: White speaks at the Republican National Convention in Cleveland, Ohio. The UFC CEO begins his address with, "What's up, GOP? ... I'm sure most of you are wondering, 'What are you doing here?'" He draws applause when he addresses why he supports Trump. "Let me tell you something: I've been in the fight business my whole life; I know fighters," White says. "Ladies and gentlemen, Donald Trump is a fighter, and I know he will fight for this country."

• Nov. 8, 2016: White and his wife, Anne, celebrate their 20th wedding anniversary in New York City and watch election night results from their hotel. When Trump is announced the winner, his son-in-law Jared Kushner calls White to invite him to Trump's victory party at the New York Hilton Midtown. White told reporters that Trump had planned to commemorate his victory at UFC 205 inside Madison Square Garden four days after getting elected. Ultimately, Trump did not attend the fights. "I don't think Donald really realized what his duties were going to be had he won," White said.

• July 11, 2017: At a prefight news conference for an upcoming Floyd Mayweather vs. Conor McGregor boxing match the UFC is promoting, White says the White House had reached out about securing tickets for the president, but ultimately Trump decided not to attend. "[Trump] feels like he'll ruin events," White says. "Secret Service is going to have to go through the place, shut down streets and create crazy traffic."

• Aug. 2, 2018: Trump hosts White and then-UFC fighter Colby Covington at the White House. In the wake of Covington's interim welterweight championship victory over Rafael dos Anjos in June, Covington and White visit the president to celebrate Covington's victory and shoot video for an upcoming UFC documentary.

• Nov. 14, 2018: UFC Fight Pass releases a mini-documentary online called "Combatant in Chief: the Story of Donald Trump's History in Combat Sports" that details White and Trump's long friendship. In a trailer for the film, which has since been removed from the UFC's channels, Trump says, "Well, there is a fighter's mentality -- whether you're in the UFC or whether or not you're president. People like Dana White have that and they have it in spades."

• Nov. 2, 2019: Trump becomes the first sitting U.S. president to attend a UFC event. As he walks out alongside White to cageside at Madison Square Garden in New York for the main card of UFC 244, headlined by Jorge Masvidal vs. Nate Diaz in the first BMF title bout, Trump is greeted by a mix of cheers and boos -- a more favorable reception than earlier in the week when Trump appeared at a World Series game in Washington to a "Lock him up!" chant from the crowd.

At the postfight news conference, White expresses no concern for the mixed reception Trump received. "This is America. You can believe and do whatever you want. If you want to boo, you can boo." he says. "... I just felt like tonight we were gonna walk in and whatever happened happened. The guy told me as a friend he would come see the fights, and he did tonight. I appreciate him, and it was a big night for the sport."

• Feb. 20, 2020: White appears at a Trump rally in Colorado Springs, Colorado, and says he and Trump have gotten closer since Trump was elected president.

• May 9, 2020: Trump congratulates White and the UFC on being the first professional sports league to resume action during the COVID-19 pandemic. "Get the sports leagues back, let's play," Trump says in a video prerecorded outside the White House's Oval Office that airs on ESPN before UFC 249. "Do the social distancing and whatever you have to do, but we need sports. We want our sports back."

• July 10, 2021: Trump attends UFC 264 at T-Mobile Arena in Las Vegas. This is his first appearance at a UFC event since the end of his first presidential run. Although Trump is in attendance, he is not shown on the broadcast. After the event, White expresses frustration with his production crew. "We were getting ready to show him right between the co-main and main events," White says in an interview with TMZ. "Let me tell you what, massive f--- up by my production team. But, you know, it's live TV and these things happen."

• Dec. 29, 2021: White appears on "The Fight with Teddy Atlas" podcast and recounts his appearance for Trump at the 2016 Republican National Convention. He reveals that his decision to appear was not popular among his associates. "Everybody, and I mean f---ing everybody, told me not to do it," White says. "I'm like, 'Are you crazy, man?' Yeah, there's no f---ing way in hell I'm not doing that for him. Then, once I spoke, you know, our friendship went to a whole 'nother level."

• April 8, 2023: After nearly two years without appearing at a UFC fight card, Trump makes an unannounced appearance at UFC 287 at Kaseya Center in Miami four days after he pleaded not guilty in New York to 34 felony counts of falsifying business records related to a cover-up of an extramarital affair. He walks to his seat flanked by White and another of his friends, musician Kid Rock, whose "American Bad Ass" plays in the arena. As he takes his cageside seat, the crowd stands, cheers and chants "U-S-A." It's the first of six UFC events he will watch in person during his second presidential campaign.

• Nov. 14, 2023: White appears on an episode of Theo Von's "This Past Weekend" podcast. White says he refused to take down a promotional video for Trump from his personal social media accounts after a "big" UFC sponsor asked him to. "Don't ever f---ing call me and tell me who to vote for," he rails.

• June 1, 2024: Two days after he is found guilty in New York on 34 felony counts, Trump is cageside for UFC 302 in Newark, New Jersey. The video of Trump and White walking to the cage while being cheered on by the Prudential Center crowd is used to announce Trump's official TikTok account. "The President is now on TikTok," White says in the video. "It's my honor," Trump responds. Trump gained more than 2 million followers in less than 24 hours after posting the video. To date, his debut post is the second-most-viewed on Trump's TikTok.

At the time, 43% of Americans under age 30 said they got their news from TikTok, according to the Pew Research Center.

• July 13, 2024: There is an assassination attempt on Trump during a presidential campaign rally outside of Butler, Pennsylvania. "I am absolutely sick to my stomach and in complete shock," White posts to social media after receiving the news.

Two days later, White appeared on "The Pat McAfee Show," praising Trump for his resilience during the shooting. "Everybody wants to act like a tough guy, right? Well, when the s--- goes down, you find out who tough guys are and who tough guys are not," White told McAfee. "This guy is the legitimate ultimate American badass of all time. A guy takes a shot at him, he goes down, he stands up and then he starts chanting to the crowd, 'Fight, fight, fight.' I literally was blown away."

• July 18, 2024: White is the final speaker at the Republican National Convention in Milwaukee, tasked with introducing the party's presidential nominee, Trump. His position at the end of the program is notable because the job is usually is reserved for the nominee's spouse or a family member. "The fact that he asked me [to introduce him], and the fact that his family also thought it should be me, is probably one of the greatest honors of all time for me," White later told Time magazine.

• Sept. 10, 2024: During a postfight interview on an episode of "Dana White's Contender Series," White says he spoke to Trump "an hour before" Trump's presidential debate vs. the Democratic nominee Kamala Harris, which Trump said he looked at "like a heavyweight fight."

"First of all, it's the second time he has to debate. He already did a debate," White says, referring to the debate held in the summer between Trump and President Joe Biden. "They didn't like how the debate turned out. They want to kick that guy [Biden] out. He's unfit to run, yet he's still the President of the United States. Now they bring in somebody who wasn't elected to actually be in there."

• Oct. 22, 2024: YouTubers the Nelk Boys post a video with Trump on a private flight. While landing in Las Vegas, Trump calls White to say, "I'm with your favorite people, the Nelk Boys ... I let them ride in the plane, Dana. I don't let too many people ride in the plane, I'll be honest with you" before calling White "the greatest of all time."

• Oct. 27, 2024: White speaks during a Trump rally at Madison Square Garden in New York City, just before election day on Nov. 5. "Ladies and gentlemen, we are nine days away from the most important election of my lifetime," White tells the crowd. "The stakes have never been higher, and the choice has never been clearer."

• Nov. 6, 2024: Hours after Trump is elected president for a second term, White addresses the crowd at an early-morning victory party at the Palm Beach Convention Center in West Palm Beach, Florida, thanking influential podcasters and streamers Adin Ross, Theo Von, the Nelk Boys and UFC commentator Joe Rogan for their part in getting Trump reelected. Each of them platformed Trump ahead of the election.

In an interview with The New Yorker two years later, White said he had been trying to connect Rogan and Trump "for probably like six years." He also said he convinced Rogan to publicly back Trump ahead of the election.

"Early on, I started telling the president, if you stay on Fox, and only Fox, you're going to lose [the election] because most of the people on Fox are already voting for you and every other network says horrible things about you," White told The New Yorker. "You gotta start getting into podcasts."

• Nov. 7, 2024 Sports Business Journal publishes a story in which White says he has no interest serving in President Trump's administration. "Donald Trump is one of my very good friends. He did a great job in his last term as president and I know he will do an even better job the next four years," White tells SBJ. "I have no personal political aspirations."

• Nov. 16, 2024: Trump is back at MSG to take in UFC 309, his first UFC event as president-elect. In the main event, Jon Jones makes his only title defense as heavyweight champion, beating two-time champ Stipe Miocic by third-round TKO. At the postfight news conference, White is asked if Trump's election changes anything for the UFC. "I think it's positive for the world, to be honest with you," he responds. " ... I think for the whole country, it feels like somebody hit the reset button."

White later indicated that this appearance was the first time Trump had mentioned the possibility of an event at the White House. "We were at an event at Madison Square Garden and the president leaned over to me and said, 'You know what? We should do an event at the White House,'" White said. "And I said, 'Yes, yes, we should do an event at the White House.'"

• Nov. 19, 2024: White swears off politics in an interview with The New Yorker, saying, "I'm never f--ing doing this again. ... It's gross. It's disgusting. I want nothing to do with politics."

• Jan. 6, 2025: Mark Zuckerberg, a UFC fan and jiu-jitsu practitioner, appoints White to the Meta board of directors. The Associated Press suggests the move could be partly motivated by a desire to curry favor with the incoming presidential administration.

• Jan. 20, 2025: At Trump's presidential inauguration ceremony, White has a prominent seat among the 600 in the Capitol Rotunda behind presidents Bill Clinton, George W. Bush and Barack Obama.

• April 12, 2025: Trump attends UFC 314 at Kaseya Center in Miami, then UFC 316 at Prudential Center in Newark, New Jersey, two months later.

• July 3, 2025: Trump makes the first public mention of a possible UFC fight card at the White House during a rally in Des Moines, Iowa, to kick off a yearlong celebration of the 250th anniversary of the United States. Trump says he wants upward of 20,000 spectators in attendance on the White House grounds for the fights on July 4, 2026. He also states his intention to host a festival at the National Mall in Washington, D.C., and an athletic competition for high school students from across the country.

"So every one of our national parks, battlefields and historic sites are going to have special events in honor of America 250," Trump says, "And I even think we're going to have a UFC fight."

Despite Trump's announcement, a White House spokesperson says there are no more details to share. White House Press Secretary Karoline Leavitt later stated that the president was "dead serious."

• Aug. 28, 2025: Two weeks after White teased a trip to Washington to visit with Trump and his daughter Ivanka, the UFC CEO confirms that event planning with the White House is underway.

"We had a meeting at the White House, [which] could not have gone better," White says in a live video on Instagram. "It's gonna be awesome. The White House fight is on. ... I will have more details on that in the next couple of weeks."

• Oct. 5, 2025: Trump says at a celebration of the U.S. Navy's 250th anniversary that the White House fight card will take place on his 80th birthday, June 14. Earlier that week, White claimed it would cost the UFC $700,000 to replace the grass on the South Lawn after the event and that weigh-ins would be held at the Lincoln Memorial.

• Dec. 7, 2025: Trump claims that "eight or nine championship fights" will take place at the White House and that the UFC is not fielding anticipated matchups on other cards in order to book them for June 14. When asked about the matchmaking, White repeatedly says the UFC will not begin arranging White House fights until after the new year.

• March 7, 2026: The UFC announces the White House fight card matchups during UFC 326 at T-Mobile Arena in Las Vegas. Unlike Trump's prediction, the official announcement features one title fight, an interim title fight and four other bouts.

• April 11, 2026: Trump attends UFC 327 at Kaseya Center in Miami. White recounts in the postfight news conference an exchange he has with Trump, a fan of heavyweight Derrick Lewis, whom he is known to call after wins.

"About an hour ago, the president leans over to me and says, 'Why is Derrick Lewis not on the White House card?"' White recalls. "And I said, 'Hold on, Mr. President.' I stepped away and called Derrick Lewis and said, 'Derrick, the president just asked why you're not on the card. Do you want to fight on the White House card?' He said, 'Of course.'"

During the fight card, Josh Hokit is victorious against Curtis Blaydes in one of the most entertaining heavyweight fights of the year. White says in the news conference that he found Hokit getting into an ambulance after the fight and rewarded him with a matchup against Lewis on the White House card.

• April 25, 2026: Trump attends the White House Correspondents' Association Dinner for the first time as a sitting president and White is "right in front of where the president was," according to the UFC CEO. The president, vice president and their spouses are rushed out of the ballroom after gunshots ring out. White recounts to reporters that guests in the ballroom were instructed to take cover but that he did not obey. Instead, he describes an "awesome" experience.

"Inside, they started up. All of a sudden, it just started getting noisy," White tells reporters. "Tables getting flipped over, guys running in with guns and they were screaming, 'Get down!' I didn't get down -- it was f---ing awesome. I literally took every minute of it in. It was a pretty crazy, unique experience."

• May 6, 2026: Trump hosts UFC fighters on the Freedom 250 fight card in the Oval Office. Lightweight champion Ilia Topuria and his challenger, interim champion Justin Gaethje, are there with Ciryl Gane and Alex Pereira, who will fight for the interim heavyweight title. During the promotional event, Trump shows renderings of the venue on the White House's South Lawn.

"As you know, [on] June 14, we're having a big fight," Trump says. "It's never gonna happen again. It's never happened before."

• May 11, 2026: White writes a letter to Trump, asking him to implore Congress to reverse a provision within the One Big Beautiful Bill Act that places a 90% limit on gambling loss deductions. "The current law makes it irrational to bet in the United States because you could end up owing taxes even when you lose or having a tax bill that exceeds your winnings for the year," White writes. "The UFC supports a healthy, legal sports betting market to drive fan engagement, broadcast value and sponsorships. When legal betting is discouraged, it hurts the ecosystem we've spent years building in partnership with state regulators and licensed operators."

• May 29, 2026: Financial disclosures for Trump's trust fund reveal that it acquired stock in TKO Group Holdings, the parent company of UFC and WWE, on March 25, weeks after White announced the Freedom 250 fights. While the exact figure is unknown, between $15,001 and $50,000 worth of TKO stock is disclosed.

• June 1, 2026: Trump tells Fox News that "you'll never see it again" in reference to the White House hosting Freedom 250 and that he's anticipating high viewership ratings. "Dana is an amazing man," Trump says. "He's done an amazing job, he's put together something that -- this will be the highest-rated event, maybe one of them ever in sports."

• June 14, 2026: After UFC Freedom 250 crowns Justin Gaethje lightweight champion and Ciryl Gane interim heavyweight titlist, Trump lauds the event on social media as "unbelievable" and says it was "one of the most exciting days in the history of our fabled White House."

• Nov. 7, 2026: Trump writes on Truth Social that he has offered the White House press secretary job to White, "a violent Fighter and Warrior." He asks White to bring along several UFC fighters and says, "Dana will be a Press Secretary like none other. Dana, please take the job!" CNN, citing a source familiar with the matter, reports that White is not taking the job. White, asked about the job offer during a Zuffa Boxing news conference in London, says he is flying to Washington to meet with Trump on Monday. "I got a lot of jobs already," White says.

• Nov. 8, 2026: After a flood of incredulous reactions on news analysis television shows and mockery on social media to his job offer to White, Trump tells reporters he was "only kidding." Speaking on an airport tarmac in West Palm Beach, Florida, before boarding a plane for Washington, Trump says, "Well, if you looked at-- you saw the assistants I put, I posted the greatest wrestlers and UFC fighters in the world, right? Like, Khabib [Nurmagomedov]. Like Dustin-- Justin Gaethje, who's phenomenal. And you see a lot of rough faces there. And you would have thought that people would have said, 'He's having a good time.' I will tell you, I was only kidding. But Dana loves the idea. And there's only one Dana, he's great, I don't know. He would be-- you wouldn't mess around with him so much. But, so, I was kidding, of course. ... That was an example of something where I was kidding and then people said, 'You know, that's actually a pretty good idea.'"

• Nov. 9, 2026: After telling TMZ he is in Washington to have Trump sign a UFC Freedom 250 trading card, White joins the president in the White House briefing room, and Trump invites him to the lectern to take questions from the media. "I've always wanted to do this: Who has the first question?" White says, smiling. "I have zero political aspirations." A reporter asks him who would win a cage fight between Trump and former President Joe Biden, and White points to Trump and calls him "the toughest, most resilient human being that I have ever met in my entire life." Asked by another reporter if he declined Trump's job offer, White says, "I don't tell the president no to anything." As the briefing is closing, Trump again asks White if he'll become press secretary or "do you just want to stay with this ridiculous UFC?" White finally says no. "Thank you for the offer, sir. I do not want to be in politics, no."

stories.headline: CF Montréal owner Joey Saputo announces club is up for sale
stories.summary: CF Montréal owner Joey Saputo announced Monday that he has initiated the sale of the MLS club his family founded in 1992.
stories.body:
CF Montréal owner Joey Saputo announced he will initiate the process of sale for the Major League Soccer club.

"After more than three decades of commitment, we believe this is the appropriate time to begin the process of identifying new ownership for CF Montréal," Saputo said on Monday. "This club has been a central part of our lives."

The Saputo family first founded the Montreal Impact in 1992 before the club became the Canadian MLS team CF Montréal in 2012.

"We have dedicated significant time, energy and resources to building it, and we are proud of what CF Montréal has become. I would also like to thank the fans, whose passion and loyalty have been at the heart of this club," Saputo said.

"We believe this is the right time to welcome a new ownership group with the resources, vision and commitment to build on the strong foundation we have established and carry forward the club's proud legacy."

Montréal concluded the 2026 regular season in last place of the Eastern Conference table with 26 points and just six wins in 34 games. The team fired head coach Marco Donadel in April after a slow start to the season, letting go of Montreal's 11th manager in 14 seasons.

Saputo confirmed the team will continue to be operational until a sale is confirmed.

Saputo added he prefers the team be sold to a local buyer, but cannot control if the team relocates to another market.

"If the club doesn't find a local buyer and I get an offer where the club needs to be relocated, then I have no choice. That is the decision I will take," he said. "Our clear preference is to find a buyer who shares our commitment to Montréal and who will ensure the club remains in the city."

The Saputo family has retained BMO Capital Markets as lead financial advisor and National Bank Financial as co-advisor to manage the sale process and identify potential buyers.

The club announced that day-to-day operations will continue as usual throughout the selling period.

stories.headline: 'The World Cup never really ended': U.S.-based betting sees rise in wagering on MLS, European soccer
stories.summary: Before the World Cup, many wondered if Americans would stick around afterward. Betting data says yes, they did.
stories.body:
Soccer was the sport of the summer in the United States this year, as the FIFA World Cup came to 11 American cities (in addition to venues in Canada and Mexico). Americans embraced the sport fully, supporting tremendous numbers for television viewership and stadium attendance -- as well as sports betting handle.

BetMGM said that the World Cup "nearly kept pace with the MLB's rigorous summer schedule" despite there being five times as many baseball games over that time period. Hard Rock Bet noted the tournament did three times as much handle and brought in double the number of individual bettors as the men's NCAA tournament, which is traditionally the most-bet-on event on the U.S. sports calendar.

In Colorado, which breaks down betting revenue by sport, the World Cup generated $60.2 million, a near 250% increase from the $17.5 million brought in by the previous edition of the tournament in November 2022.

With European league soccer in full swing and Major League Soccer kicking off playoffs, that momentum has continued over for the American sports betting ecosystem.

BetMGM noted that in the two-month period immediately following the conclusion of the 2026 World Cup, the sportsbook saw a 24.5% year-over-year increase in bets and a 34.5% increase in handle on wagers for club soccer. Hard Rock said there have been nearly 30% more wagers on soccer overall, specifically 43% more in the Premier League and 21% in the Champions League with World Cup stars Kylian Mbappé, Erling Haaland and Harry Kane attracting double the amount of bets in the competition compared to the same time period last year.

"The World Cup never really ended for our customers. The bettors who did well backing Mbappé, Haaland and Kane this summer have followed them straight back to the Champions League, and the post-World Cup pain continues for us every time those guys light up the scoreboard," Hard Rock Bet SVP of sportsbook Neil Walsh told ESPN over email. "Those Tuesday and Wednesday afternoon matches don't compete with primetime U.S. sports, so they get our customers' full attention."

"We have seen an immediate increase in activity across our soccer markets when comparing 2026 with 2025," Caesars lead soccer trader Mark Bickerdike said in an email.

"Encouragingly, that growth is evident across both pre-match and in-play betting and is reflected across the majority of competitions we offer. It certainly feels as though we've benefited from the momentum generated by the World Cup heading into the new domestic seasons."

MLS has attracted significantly more betting action in 2026 than it did the year before, showing a 30.4% increase in tickets and a 38.8% increase in money from mid-July to the end of October. MLS handle is up 27% at Hard Rock Bet over a similar time period, with Inter Miami -- a fixture for the Florida-based book -- garnering almost 40% more bets year-over-year.

"We've seen a jump up in more users that are betting soccer and a lot of that is from MLS," DraftKings director of sports operations Johnny Avello told ESPN. "We'd like to think that's from people betting the World Cup this year and finding out that soccer's a fun game to wager on."

The development of MLS' betting market comes in the wake of unprecedented popularity for the league and as it looks to transition to a fall-spring schedule that lines up with the rest of world soccer.

Bickerdike said that since Aug. 1, MLS has moved from being Caesars' fourth-most bet soccer league to second. The revised calendar could benefit the league further.

"It creates the opportunity for customers to engage with a full day of soccer, starting with competitions such as the Premier League and LaLiga before moving into a slate of MLS fixtures later in the day," said Bickerdike. "From a sportsbook perspective, our market offering is consistent across these competitions, creating a seamless experience for customers and potentially encouraging greater engagement with MLS over time."

Coming out of MLS Decision Day on Saturday, Nashville SC are the favorites for the MLS Cup at +400. Thomas Müller's Vancouver Whitecaps and Lionel Messi's Inter Miami (the reigning champions) follow just behind at +450.

stories.headline: Wings' Paige Bueckers, Azzi Fudd talk relationship on pod
stories.summary: Azzi Fudd hosted Wings teammate Paige Bueckers on her podcast and the two discussed their relationship, Dallas' season and Fudd's recovery from knee surgery.
stories.body:
Dallas Wings teammates Azzi Fudd and Paige Bueckers, the past two WNBA No. 1 draft picks, spoke on Fudd's podcast Friday about a variety of topics, including a personal life update.

"We're not together anymore; it's been a while," Bueckers said on the "Fudd Around and Find Out" podcast. "[We] share that because everybody [was] like, 'Oh my gosh, they're teammates, how is this going to work?'"

Bueckers and Fudd, who were teammates in college at UConn, said they felt the need to address their relationship status in part because of allegations it factored into the Wings picking Fudd at No. 1 in April. Fudd was chosen over TCU guard Olivia Miles, who went on to be the Rookie of the Year for the Minnesota Lynx. Spain's Awa Fam (Seattle Storm) was taken third, followed by teammates from the 2026 champion UCLA Bruins: Lauren Betts (Washington Mystics), Gabriela Jaquez (Chicago Sky) and Kiki Rice (Toronto Tempo).

Fudd, Fam, Betts and Miles were all No. 1 at different points in ESPN's mock draft in the months before the April draft. Bueckers said her previous relationship with Fudd had no impact on Dallas' decision.

"We were not together before she got drafted," Bueckers said. "She was not drafted because she was my girlfriend. She was drafted because she deserved it. She's an amazing human, an amazing basketball player. And we're still friends, we're still cool.

"We played an entire season together; we're the utmost professionals."

Fudd averaged 13.1 points but was limited to just 30 games after an injury to her right knee led to season-ending arthroscopic surgery in August. She offered an update on her health.

"My offseason's been good," Fudd said. "Lots of rehab, lots of training, lots of on-court workouts, lots of traveling. It's been busy.

"I think there's a lot I can improve on. Especially the iso game; I feel like I'm not too comfortable with that yet. I know I'm capable of doing a little bit more. Watching someone like Paige who is able to create from anywhere ... that's great inspiration for me."

Bueckers averaged 20.9 points, 4.1 rebounds and 5.9 assists, and was named to the All-WNBA second team as Dallas reached the playoffs as the No. 7 seed.

The Wings were eliminated in the first round by the eventual champion Golden State Valkyries. Bueckers said she learned a lot from her first playoff experience and complimented Golden State.

"The Valkyries' defense, I can't explain to you how tough they are," Bueckers said. "They swarm, they send bodies, they trap you, they blitz you, they're so connected. I'm glad I got to have that experience against them to open my eyes to what the playoffs are like -- the physicality, the pressure, the environment.

"And I'm proud of our season. I hated losing; I sat and was pissed about it for like a week. I reached out to [Sue Bird] about it, what was her first playoff experience like. I didn't play as well as I wanted to. But it was my first experience, going against a really good opponent, and I was learning and growing through it all."

Fudd and Bueckers also addressed the Wings' move to the 19,000-seat American Airlines Center in downtown Dallas next season after playing at UT Arlington's College Park Center, which seats over 7,000, since the franchise relocated to Texas in 2016.

"UTA was a vibe; we had a ball, we did our thing there," Bueckers said. "But definitely excited to move into Dallas. New times."

While the change in venue will lead to more eyes on Wings games, the two players said they're hoping for less scrutiny of any on-court behavior.

Both said fans shouldn't read into interactions the two have with each other or their teammates as anything other than normal team behavior. They also said they don't stand for "hate of any kind" or "tearing people down to lift us up."

"We've seen a lot of negativity," Bueckers said. "We've had stuff sent to us, stuff sent to our family, our friends. There's been some crazy things said about us. We still support each other, we're still going to be great friends, we're still going to be great teammates. All the negative things can be put aside, and you don't need to overanalyze everything."

Fudd added with a chuckle, "Also, we don't need messages [from fans] on what the other person's doing. We've addressed everything we need to, and the rest will stay with us."

Eventually they proved to be too good for Fiji, who were unable to maintain the intensity over the full journey.

New Zealand were completely dominant in their defeat of Samoa, running in 32 unanswered points. Stacey Waaka scored a hat trick which showcased her elusiveness and pure speed out wide. In defence the Kiwis Ferns smothered any attempt by Samoa to unleash their backline. Up the middle New Zealand carved a path to allow their halves the space to take control.

The Kiwi Ferns will have to do all of that and more, if they are to threaten the Jillaroos' dominance. There is something inevitable about the Australians, across the park are stars of the game and at fullback one of the finest in Tamika Upton. The first try to Tom Dearden came from a scrum 10 metres out, and 10 metres in from the left sideline, with Australia setting up a complex array of backline threats to the right. The Samoan defence seemed so mesmerised by what was in front of them, that the last thing they expected was a dummy and a step of his right foot to see halfback Dearden clean through. As the game progressed those backline threats were put to work in similar patterns and Samoa had very few answers.

Kevin Walters has settled on Reece Walsh at fullback and although he had a mixed game defensively against Samoa, his attacking spark was undeniable. Cameron Munster was inspirational in directing the team, and taking the hard hits when plays broke down. Last week New Zealand welcomed Kalyn Ponga back after his three-week recovery from a broken arm, and he was masterful in dismantling the Tongan defence. New Zealand have improved enough with the ball to take better advantage of any forward momentum in the final.

This should be a cracking final, with both teams peaking at the right time. My head is suggesting that the Kiwis will be too strong, but my heart is saying Australia always seem to get the job done.

stories.headline: Josh Allen and the Bills move to 7-1 with a 23-6 win over the sputtering Vikings
stories.summary: — The Buffalo Bills knew they weren't bound for many style points or likely to reach their league-leading scoring average against Minnesota's relentlessly...
stories.body:
MINNEAPOLIS -- — The Buffalo Bills knew they weren't bound for many style points or likely to reach their league-leading scoring average against Minnesota's relentlessly revved-up defense.


Josh Allen, James Cook and the rest of the group were more than content to grind this one out.


Allen threw a touchdown pass with 44 seconds left before halftime and Cook had 31 carries for 107 yards and a late score for the Bills in a 23-6 victory on Monday night, sending Vikings deeper into an unmitigated offensive slump.


“We stuck with it, stuck with it, and eventually we broke it,” Cook said. “We knew what type of game it was going to be, a bloody game."


With Kyler Murray sidelined by a hamstring injury, Carson Wentz started at quarterback for the Vikings (6-2) and didn’t finish what became one of the worst performances of his 11-year career.


Linebackers Terrel Bernard and Dorian Williams had interceptions and Tyler Bass made three field goals to stretch his franchise-record streak to 24 straight as the Bills (7-1) matched their best eight-game start since 1993. That season ended with the last of their four straight Super Bowl losses.


"It’s just a mindset of going out there and not being result-driven, going out there and being process-driven and understanding what they’re trying to do," said Allen, who went 21 for 31 for 234 yards and one interception. “At the end of the day, having fun playing the game of football.”


The Vikings as usual sent blitzers at Allen from every angle possible, racking up four sacks. Allen heaved a third-and-23 throw into the end zone to beat the rush in the first quarter that Byron Murphy ran down and returned 55 yards. But the Bills eked out just enough in the first half to give themselves a lead, when Allen found tight end Keleki Latu open in the back of the end zone for a 25-yard touchdown as he rolled right and was hit hard by Andrew Van Ginkel.


“There was no panic early in the game when things weren’t going our way,” coach Joe Brady said, marveling at his team's 42:32 possession time. “Eventually you end up making it a game that they weren’t willing to play.”


The Vikings are running out of answers on offense
Wentz went 8 for 25 for 81 yards and three turnovers, including a backward pass in the first quarter that was thrown too high for even Justin Jefferson to catch it — resulting in a lost fumble near midfield.


Wentz, who was checked out in the medical tent at one point for an apparent lower leg injury, was replaced by Max Brosmer midway through the fourth quarter. Wentz completed 1 of 8 passes in the second half, and the Vikings finished with just 178 total yards.


The battle between the best offense and best defense in the NFL might well have gone to Minnesota had the offense been able to muster a decent drive or two.


But the Vikings had four straight possessions in the first half start beyond their 40-yard line, and the furthest they made it was the Bills 48.


“Put tonight 100% on me. It’s not about any one particular player," Vikings coach Kevin O'Connell said. "But we’ve got to improve offensively, at a rapid pace.”


O'Connell blamed himself for not calling more running plays: Jordan Mason and Aaron Jones combined for just 11 carries when it was clear from the start how off-the-mark Wentz was. Jefferson finished with three catches for 58 yards on 11 targets.


“I've always said it doesn’t really matter who’s throwing the ball, as long as it gets there,” Jefferson said. "That’s all that matters. It’s up to us to make those plays. It’s tough, definitely tough.”


Allen matches Manning's 10-year touchdown mark
With 322 regular-season touchdowns — 232 passing, 88 rushing and two receiving — Allen tied Peyton Manning for the most in NFL history over a player's first 10 years. Allen is halfway through his ninth season.


Injury report
Bills: Starting LT Dion Dawkins (ribs) and starting LG Alec Anderson (ankle) were inactive.


Vikings: WR Jauan Jennings (calf) and FS Theo Jackson (quadriceps) were inactive.


Up next
Bills: At the New York Jets on Sunday.


Vikings: At Green Bay on Sunday.

stories.headline: Sources: Man United turn to U.S. coach Pochettino with Carrick on the brink
stories.summary: United States coach Mauricio Pochettino is the favored candidate to replace Michael Carrick as Manchester United manager, sources have told ESPN.
stories.body:
United States coach Mauricio Pochettino is the favored candidate to replace Michael Carrick as Manchester United manager with the club ready to fire the 45-year-old due to growing alarm over the team dropping into the Premier League relegation zone, sources have told ESPN.

The United hierarchy, led by co-chairman Joel Glazer, minority owner Jim Ratcliffe, CEO Omar Berrada and director of football Jason Wilcox, is assessing Carrick's position after the club's worst-ever start to a Premier League season left United just one point off the bottom of the table having won once in 10 league games to date.

- Ogden: Ratcliffe chose to appoint rookies at Man United, and it has them facing relegation﻿ fight

While sources have said discussions are ongoing and will continue over the coming days, they have also told ESPN that there is now acceptance that performances and results demand a change of manager.

Pochettino, 54, extended his contract with the U.S. Soccer Federation until 2030 in August after guiding the United States to the round of 16 at the World Cup this summer.

A source told ESPN that the former Tottenham, Chelsea and Paris Saint-Germain coach has an escape clause in his contract with the U.S. for $10 million (£7.4 million), which Man United would have to pay for the Argentine's services.

Former Newcastle manager Eddie Howe is another candidate admired by United bosses. Julian Nagelsmann, who is also currently out of work, is among the options, and Kieran McKenna, who was interviewed for the job in 2024, has supporters at Old Trafford.

But it is Pochettino -- who has interviewed for the United job on three previous occasions -- who is regarded as having the Premier League experience and personality needed to drag United out of danger and revive the club's fortunes.

Carrick signed a two-year contract at United in the summer after guiding the club to Champions League qualification following his arrival as interim manager in January.

Sources have said that United believed Carrick, whose only previous managerial experience was with Championship team Middlesbrough, merited a long-term deal after his success at Old Trafford last season.

But senior figures have been shocked by the drop in performances and results this season. After they gave the former United midfielder time to turn around the situation last month, Carrick has been able to win only one of four games since his reprieve, and sources have said that his prospects are now increasingly bleak.

United are next in action against Liverpool at Anfield on Nov. 22.

- Neville on Carrick's Man United future: 'Ownership don't have a clue'

State of play and players to know
Essendon will be on the clock first, holding the top selection a decade on from the last time it took the number one pick to the AFL Draft. The Dons are expected to first bid on Port Adelaide-tied forward Dougie Cochrane, which will trigger a start-of-second-round compensation pick for the Bombers, Tigers and Eagles.

There are familial lines drawn throughout an exciting 2008-born cohort. Cody Walker is the son of high-flying Blue Andrew and will be headed to Princes Park. Cochrane is the son of former North Melbourne and Port Adelaide midfielder Stuart, though he isn't eligible to either team under the 100-game father-son rule. Instead, he's eligible to join the Power as part of their Next Generation Academy as an Indigenous prospect.

Top-10 riser Sam Gayfer is the nephew of 1990 premiership Pie Mick, and Koby LeCras brings goalkicking pedigree via 2018 premiership uncle Mark.

There will be up to five club-tied talents picked in the first round of the AFL Draft. But that won't necessarily result in an extended first night. Over the past five years the first round has averaged out to 25 selections accounting for father-son and academy bids, but clubs are expecting a number closer to the traditional 18 picks in the final intake of the 18-team competition.

Stricter stipulations around matching bids is at play, with clubs only able to use a maximum of two selections when matching for a club-tied prospect, meaning the selections of Port Adelaide, Carlton, Brisbane and GWS will be absorbed as early bids are matched.

We could see a record number of Indigenous talents picked in the first round. The high-water mark was four in 2005 and 2014, and all of Cochrane, Walker, Caylen Murray (Lions Academy), Toby Krasna and Jake Eime could be taken in the first round in 2026.

Thirteen of the top prospects have already been invited to Marvel Stadium on November 19.

Ethan Drever, Arki Butler and Heath Mellody are all still in contention to be the open pool No. 1 pick, with Harry Van Hattum, Gus Teixeira, Mitch Harris and Ethan Matthews (Giants Academy) rounding out the group on top of draft boards alongside Cochrane and Walker.

Around 65 picks are expected to be taken across both nights which would surpass the 60 selections last year.

stories.headline: Who has won MLB Rookie of the Year? All-time winners list
stories.summary: MLB's Rookie of the Year award is presented to the best rookies of the American and National League. Check out the full list of winners by year.
stories.body:
In 1947 and 1948, the Rookie of the Year was given to Major League Baseball's top rookie-eligible player. Since 1949, the award has been presented to a player in the American League and National League. The Baseball Writers' Association of America votes on the award at the end of each season and before the start of the postseason.

Before 1957, voters used their own judgment to determine which players were considered rookies. After 1957, players were considered rookies if they had fewer than 75 at-bats or 45 innings pitched prior to the season. This was later changed to 90 at-bats, 45 innings pitched or 45 days of MLB service time. In 1971, the mark was adjusted to 130 at-bats, 50 innings pitched or 45 days of non-September service time. That remains the standard today.

Jackie Robinson was MLB's first Rookie of the Year in 1947. Robinson hit .297 with 12 home runs, 31 doubles, five triples, 48 RBIs and 29 stolen bases for the Brooklyn Dodgers. The award has been named the Jackie Robinson Award since 1987, the 40th anniversary of Robinson breaking the league's color barrier.

stories.headline: Toto Wolff: Mercedes face fierce 2027 battle after winning constructors' title
stories.summary: Mercedes team principal Toto Wolff has played down the suggestion his team is about to embark on another period of dominance in Formula 1, and believes the battle for the 2027 title has already started.
stories.body:
Mercedes team principal Toto Wolff has played down the suggestion his team is about to embark on another period of dominance in Formula 1, and believes the battle for the 2027 title has already started.

They sealed the constructors' championship with three races of the season remaining at the Sao Paulo Grand Prix on Sunday, just one week after Kimi Antonelli secured the drivers' championship in Mexico City.

The German manufacturer stole a march on its rivals at the start of the year following the introduction of new engine regulations and has continued to be competitive throughout the season.

But after winning just one race in the last five, Wolff believes rival teams Red Bull, McLaren and Ferrari are in a position to pose a serious threat for the title in 2027.

"Look at the last few races, we haven't won," Wolff said. "And today at the beginning of the race, Kimi was just storming away, it looked like this could be ours, but the competition has been getting tougher, between Ferrari, McLaren, Red Bull and ourselves.

"It's four teams that can win races and will be challenging for a world championship. And I have no doubt that it's going to be very difficult for us next year.

"So for me, the 2027 season has started now. It is about learning in the three last races.

"What is it we can optimise? What didn't we spot when we put the upgrade on the car? What is it we can learn from today, and attack these last three races full blast, whilst also making sure that we have the learning for next year's power unit and next year's car."

Wolff believes the sheer quality of the top teams on the grid means the era of runaway teams in new regulations cycles -- such as Mercedes from 2014 and Red Bull from 2022 -- is a thing of the past.

"It looks like the most competitive era that is about to start, because the teams have become so professional in capability, in resource, that these kind of runaway seasons, I don't see them anymore, whether it's four in a row or eight in a row," he said. "And that is a completely new challenge.

"You can see how quickly it goes from being dominant and within a few races you realise that your upgrade doesn't work and you fall back and you're just third on the road. So it's great for the sport.

"I wish it was the era of Mercedes and me running away with another few titles, but I don't think it's the reality."

- Wet weather mastery by Norris, Verstappen makes Brazil F1's must-see race

- Mercedes completes the double with constructors' title at São Paulo Grand Prix

Wolff believes one of the keys to Mercedes' success remains its no-blame culture and its ability to empower its employees.

"We have stability certainly as a factor, but we have also many people that have joined us recently, and I think what I would like to choose as a word is safety. We are not a high-and-fire organisation.

"We provide a culture and an environment where you can thrive, where you are allowed to make mistakes, where you can speak up. And over the long term, I believe, if you want to be successful, not over a period of a few years, but over many decades, this is what you need to be able to kind of ingrain in the team. And we're trying that.

"It's not something you put on a PowerPoint. You have to live those standards in and out. These are the standards we are setting for ourselves.

"Sometimes we fail, but we look at the long-term vision. For me, soon is in ten years, and I need to set the team up for soon."
